subject: EU-West Dedicated Pool Stall — Mitigation, Credits & Next Steps
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@finberg.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finberg SRE <sre@finberg.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T07:30:00Z
Subject: High error rate + stuck jobs in EU-West cluster

Hi Diego,

We started seeing a spike in throttled requests at ~07:15 UTC and by 07:22 several of our batch jobs went to 'stalled' in your EU-West dedicated pool. The jobs did not auto-retry and users hit timeouts. Can you confirm whether this is a service-side degradation? Our SRE attached a short log excerpt.

Immediate asks:
- Status and ETA for resolution
- Whether this triggers SLA credits for the outage window
- Any mitigation we should perform on our side (retries, alternate region routing)

Attachment: job_log_excerpt.txt (text/plain)

Thanks,
Nora
Head of Platform
Finberg.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T07:45:00Z
Subject: Fwd: High error rate + stuck jobs in EU-West cluster — triage

Team, forwarding Finberg's report. Quick summary from initial telemetry:
- Autoscaler entered a throttle mode due to an unexpected spike in ephemeral node warmups combined with a recent maintenance window that reduced headroom.
- Several nodes reported slow initialization (NV driver & container warmup) causing request queues to pile and request-level timeouts.
- No evidence of noisy customer requests from their side; patterns point to warmup + allocator pressure.

Immediate action items:
1) Marissa / Connor: open a bridge and spin a temporary reserved node increment (+2) in eu-west to relieve queued work.
2) Neha: capture allocator traces and the autoscaler decision log between 07:00-07:40 UTC. Attach initial_observation.log here.
3) Grace: prepare a customer-facing mitigation note with ETA and proposed credit offer.

Attachment: initial_observation.log (text/plain)

I'll monitor and will update Finberg once we have the reserved nodes in place.

— Diego
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Patel <nora@finberg.ai>, Finberg SRE <sre@finberg.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T09:10:00Z
Subject: RE: EU-West Dedicated Pool Stall — short-term mitigation and credit proposal

Hi Nora,

Apologies for the disruption this morning — thank you for the log excerpt, that helped speed diagnostics. Quick update on what we did and next steps:

What we did (07:45–08:30 UTC):
- Provisioned two temporary reserved nodes in eu-west and routed Finberg's tenant to the nodes (should reduce queuing immediately).
- Increased autoscaler soft-limits to prevent premature throttle while we investigate warmup variance.
- Applied a short-term kernel-level warmup tweak to reduce container init latency for common CUDA images.

Impact: your queued jobs started progressing around 08:05 UTC and by 08:30 the backlog was cleared. We continued monitoring for two hours; tail errors have normalized.

Credit proposal: as a gesture of goodwill we propose a one-off credit equal to 12 hours of reserved capacity at your current committed rate. We'll formalize the number in the next update and can route the credit through procurement.

Next steps (we own):
- Root cause analysis & postmortem doc (shared within 72 hours) — action items and timeline for a permanent fix.
- Follow-up runbook that prevents similar warmup cascades (Connor + Neha).
- Longer-term: consider a warm standby headroom setting for your Dedicated pool (we can provide a cost/benefit estimate).

Attachment: mitigation_timeline.pdf (application/pdf)

Please let us know if the mitigation looks sufficient from your perspective or if you saw any remaining anomalies.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Nora Patel <nora@finberg.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finberg SRE <sre@finberg.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T11:02:00Z
Subject: RE: EU-West Dedicated Pool Stall — short-term mitigation and credit proposal

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick remediation.

A couple of clarifying points for our side:
- Confirm the exact outage window you will use to calculate credits (we observed 07:15–08:05 UTC as impacted).
- Can you confirm whether the warmup tweak is a temporary patch or a permanent config change? We want assurance this won't be reversed during future maintenance windows.
- We expect a formal postmortem we can share with our executive and procurement teams. The postmortem should include impact summary, timeline, RCA, permanent remediation plan, and the credit calculation.

Once we have that we can close our incident internally.

Regards,
Nora

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: EU-West Dedicated Pool Stall — mitigation, credits & next steps (internal summary)

Internal summary and commitments to finish today:

1) Credit finalization (Marissa): compute credit using Finberg's observed window 07:15–08:05 UTC; convert to reserved-hour equivalent and draft the formal credit CSV. Deliverable: credit_proposal.csv attached.
2) Postmortem (Neha/Connor): collect allocator traces, autoscaler decision logs, driver init variance. Draft postmortem doc link saved to Drive and shared in related_links. Deliverable: postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow; final version within 72 hours.
3) Runbook & config changes (Connor): implement the warm standby headroom change as a configurable parameter and gate it behind per-tenant cost opt-in; provide cost/benefit for Finberg.
4) Customer comms (Marissa): send formal postmortem and credit paperwork to procurement once items 1–2 are ready.

Attachment: credit_proposal.csv (text/csv)
Forwarded: "Marissa's mitigation timeline" quoted below for context.
